children.text: Saving shows only once the save has run for 500 ms (owner, 2026-11-02, #1553), on both screens. A faster save goes straight to Safe to switch off, or to Restarting when an update installs: a screen shows only when it tells the player something, and a face that is gone within half a second tells them nothing. On the console the largest saved session (144 MB) writes with fsync in about 250 ms, so most saves never show it; each save logs "power: saved in N ms" so the threshold can be tuned. During a fast save the main screen draws nothing new but takes no touch, and the 7" readout keeps the track display. Why a step list on a slow save: a face that only says "Saving…" gives no sign that it is still moving, so the player cannot tell a slow disk from a hang, and switching off then loses the session. The rows are the real stages of the save, in order: playback stopped (the transport stops), settings saved (the settings flush), writing the session (the session file) and finishing on disk (storage writes settle and the installer is asked once more). None is invented. An empty unnamed session writes nothing, so its list has no "Writing the session" row and its headline is just "Saving". Done rows show a green check, the current row a spinner, later rows a muted ring. The 440 x 8 bar fills with the finished rows. The readout shows "Saving", the current row and the same bar.
